notable_absence.finding: The page recommends a starting nofile value of 250000 but explicitly declines to give a fixed minimum: 'There is no single fixed minimum, but the default OS limit of `1024` is insufficient for any production deployment.' This is a rare case of the documentation stating outright that it CANNOT give a firm default/minimum for a production-critical setting, rather than simply omitting one.

cross_component_finding: This page names THREE separate, independently-configured file-descriptor ceiling layers that all apply simultaneously to the same running Sync Gateway process - the OS-wide fs.file-max, the per-process/per-container ulimit (nofile), Sync Gateway's own max_file_descriptors setting, and (for systemd deployments specifically) systemd's hardcoded LimitNOFILE=65535 - and states plainly that raising the Sync-Gateway-level setting has zero effect unless the OS/container/systemd ceiling is raised too. command-line-options.md (this batch) documents only the innermost of these four layers with no default value at all; this page is where the full stack and the actual default (5000) are documented.
cross_product_finding: The container-vs-host distinction this page draws ('For container environments... see Container Environments... The host-level instructions below are geared towards CentOS deployments') and its explicit ownership hand-off ('This means your Infra or Platform team, rather than the application team, typically owns this configuration') is OS/infrastructure-layer guidance with no Couchbase-Server-side analogue referenced anywhere in this batch - Sync Gateway's own OS tuning guide stands alone rather than pointing at a parallel Couchbase Server OS-tuning page, unlike deployment.md's swappiness recommendation (same batch), which DOES cross-reference a Couchbase Server install guide for the identical kind of OS-level advice.
